newsitem.title: USA: Americans upbeat on stocks as long-haul investment.
newsitem.headline: Americans upbeat on stocks as long-haul investment.

text.p: American investors are cautiously upbeat about stocks despite a long-running bull market, and most say they wouldn't bail out in the event of a significant downturn, a new NASDAQ survey shows.

The survey, conducted for NASDAQ between January 11 and 18 by Peter D. Hart Research Associates, showed that 63 percent of investors expect stock prices to rise over the next 12 months, with 58 percent anticipating a moderate increase and 20 percent expecting a strong increase.
The survey includes a sample of 1,009 investors, with 103 more interviews of young investors and 102 of new investors.
Most investors (54 percent) said these are "good times" for investing in stocks, while only nine percent said this is a "bad time" to invest.
NASDAQ said investors were only slightly more optimistic on this question now than they were in the June 1988 poll conducted for NASDAQ following the 1987 stock market crash.
The survey indicated that 54 percent of investors would not make any major changes to their stock holdings in the event of a significant stock market decline.

Of those investors surveyed, 44 percent said they invest in stocks and mutual funds beucase "over the long run, stocks consistently outperform other investments," while only six percent said they are attracted to stocks because of the recent runup in prices.
